title: Bigos
subtitle: Polish hunter's stew
excerpt: A slow-cooked stew of pork, smoked sausage, and bacon with braised cabbage, dried mushrooms, and red wine. Bigos is Poland's national dish and improves every time it is reheated. Make a large batch and eat it over several days.
sourceNotes: Bigos is Poland's national stew. It traditionally used whatever was in the hunter's bag, cooked with sauerkraut and dried mushrooms. No two versions are the same, but the base of braised cabbage and smoked meats is constant.

recipe.freezeNotes: Bigos freezes very well. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: This stew improves over several days. Make a large batch and reheat.

content.text: Bigos takes time but demands little attention once it is on the heat. The combination of smoked meat, slow-braised cabbage, and earthy dried mushrooms is uniquely satisfying. It gets better each time you reheat it.

items.prepNote: shredded -- use sauerkraut if available, rinse lightly first
soaked in 200ml hot water for 20 minutes, soaking liquid reserved

content.text: Soak dried mushrooms in 200ml hot water for 20 minutes. Drain and roughly chop -- reserve the soaking liquid, straining it through a fine sieve.
In a large pot, fry bacon and sausage until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add a little oil to the pot. Brown the pork shoulder in batches over high heat. Remove and set aside.
Add onion to the pot and cook on medium heat for 5 minutes. Add cabbage and stir until it starts to wilt.
Pour in wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add tinned tomatoes, mushrooms, strained mushroom soaking liquid, caraway seeds, and bay leaves. Return all the meats to the pot.
Cover and simmer on a low heat for 1.5 hours. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with rye bread.

items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer on a higher heat for 15-20 minutes to reduce.

content.text: Poland and across Central Europe. Traditionally made in large pots for hunting parties. Often reheated over multiple days, getting better each time. It is considered Poland's national dish. Every family and every region has its own version.
